description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, FABRICATIONS (LAUNCH SITE)

SpaceX demands a new type of supply chain. We require our suppliers to provide premium quality with rapidly evolving designs at increasingly ambitious volumes. We are actively looking for candidates who possess comprehensive knowledge of manufacturing and quality tools and have an unrelenting motivation to enable suppliers to succeed. This position will be the key focal point for heavy fabrications on Starship launch infrastructure and ground support equipment, and requires a combination of proven leadership and technical capabilities. 

This is a highly technical position that requires practical experience in process engineering and new product introduction through stabilized production for large and heavy welded fabrications used on Starship launch infrastructure and ground support equipment. The ideal candidate will have a broad understanding of structural steel fabrication, welding, non-destructive evaluation, and coating systems for structures such as launch mounts, launch towers, and large storage tanks, with the desire and capability to take on new challenges in unfamiliar areas to help enable our mission to Mars. 

RESPONSIBILITIES: 

  • Act as the technical point of contact for assigned large and heavy fabrications within flight, non-flight, and launch-site and recovery infrastructure, solving emergent challenges at suppliers and mitigating risk to the manifest by addressing high-impact fabrication, welding, and quality issues
  • Lead and coordinate containment activities for structural weldments, launch mounts, tower sections, and other heavy fabrications to protect build, erection, and launch schedules, and drive ongoing reliability improvements in the fabrications supply base
  • Intervene and drive resolution at the supplier for critical-path fabricated structures to ensure zero disruption to site construction, integration, and operations
  • Review issues on assigned fabrications and solve to the root cause, implementing changes at the supplier, at SpaceX, or both; drive further actions to closure; and re-source to new suppliers where appropriate
  • Create and disposition issue tickets where needed, working with engineering counterparts on rework, repair, or use-as-is, including weld repairs, distortion, fit-up, NDE indications, and coating nonconformances
  • Become thoroughly familiar with assigned structures and the cutting, forming, welding, machining, NDE, and coating processes that make up the overall fabrication, and become the primary point of contact for supply-chain-related defects on those products
  • Work with procurement to find and qualify heavy-fabrication suppliers and vet them for weld capability, shop capacity, lifting and handling, quality systems, and ability to meet aggressive takt times
  • Conduct design-for-manufacturing and design-for-fabrication reviews of large weldments so structures are manufacturable, inspectable, and erectable early, preferably prior to sourcing, including joint design, weld access, distortion control, and inspection hold points
  • Own the new product introduction process at the supplier for new fabrications, drawing and weld-specification changes, or when re-sourcing existing structures to a new supplier
  • Drive production part approval (or an equivalent fabrication qualification package: weld procedures, welder qualifications, NDE, dimensional inspection, and coating inspection) to stabilize supply, reduce inspection oversight, and improve delivery
  • Support supplier process audits covering welding procedure and performance qualification, fit-up and distortion control, NDE, traceability, and structural coating application for launch mounts, launch towers, and large storage tanks
  • Demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, attention to detail, self-direction, and the courage to push the technical envelope conventionally held in the industry
  • Drive for results and customer satisfaction by collaborating with launch-site engineering, construction, and procurement, leading projects, and continuously improving the heavy-fabrications supply base 

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in an engineering or STEM discipline 
  • 5+ years of experience with manufacturing and/or inspection of mechanical products in a production environment 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES: 

  • Master’s degree in welding engineering, materials, civil, structural, or mechanical engineering, or a related discipline
  • Experience with large and heavy steel fabrication: plate and structural shape processing, fit-up of large weldments, subassembly and final assembly of structures such as launch mounts, towers, frames, and large storage tanks
  • Weld engineering experience, including development and review of welding procedure specifications and procedure qualification records, welder performance qualification, joint design, preheat and interpass control, and repair welding
  • Working knowledge of structural and pressure-equipment welding standards (for example AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 or D1.6 as applicable, ASME Section IX, and ASME Section VIII or API 650/620 for tank work)
  • Experience with non-destructive evaluation of welds and base metal, including visual, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, and radiographic testing, and with interpretation of NDE reports and acceptance criteria
  • Experience with structural coating systems: surface preparation, primer and topcoat systems for exterior and marine or launch-site environments, dry-film thickness, holiday detection, and coating inspection (for example SSPC/NACE practices)
  • Experience with large storage tank fabrication, including shell and floor fit-up, welding sequence, dimensional control, and associated inspection and test
  • Experience interpreting engineering drawings and models for heavy weldments, including weld symbols, GD&T, and fabrication and erection tolerances
  • Working knowledge of supplier quality processes (production part approval, advanced product quality planning, first article or in-process inspection, inspection and test plans)
  • Knowledge of statistical techniques and methods (design of experiments, Lean, Six Sigma) applied to weld quality, distortion, and fabrication throughput
  • Experience with quality systems (ISO 9001, AISC or equivalent structural fabrication quality programs, ASME, and NADCAP or equivalent where special processes apply) and manufacturing systems (MRP/ERP)
  • Working knowledge of problem-solving techniques such as 8D or A3
  • Proficient in MS Office and Excel and in report writing
  • Proficient in SQL and Power BI
  • Experience sharing information and influencing others across organizational lines, internally and at suppliers, including on the shop floor and at heavy-fabrication vendors 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

  • Must be able to travel - up to 60-85% work week travel may be required, including international travel
  • Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to meet major milestones 
  • Valid driver’s license 

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
